table.description: The name of the table the GC policy applies to.
table.rationale: Table name only identifies where GC rules apply; it does not expose credentials, grant IAM, or change who can read data by itself.

instance_name.description: The name of the Bigtable instance containing the table.
instance_name.rationale: Instance identifier for routing the policy to the right cluster; not a secret and does not by itself widen access or weaken encryption.

column_family.description: The column family this GC policy is attached to.
column_family.rationale: Schema/column-family label only; it scopes which cells the GC policy affects but does not grant principals access or leak key material.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Project ID is non-secret scope metadata for API calls; it does not replace IAM checks or expose table contents.

mode.description: How multiple GC rules combine: `intersection` or `union`.
mode.rationale: Controls how rule predicates are combined mathematically; it does not name principals or secrets and is not an access-control mechanism by itself.

max_age.description: Age-based retention block for the GC rule (evaluated as `max_age.days` or duration fields per provider).
max_age.rationale: The block is only a container in Terraform; it holds no secret values. Retention risk is expressed in nested fields such as `days`, which are evaluated separately for security impact.

days.description: Maximum age of cells to retain, in days.
days.rationale: Longer retention increases how long stale or sensitive cell history may remain recoverable (`max_age.days`).

duration.description: Alternative duration representation for max age when used instead of `days`.
duration.rationale: Another encoding for the same retention length as `days`; whichever field is used, the sensitive governance question is the retention value, not the fact that this alternate attribute exists.

max_version.description: Version-based retention block for the GC rule.
max_version.rationale: Structural wrapper only; it does not expose credentials. Version-count limits that affect data lifetime are in nested `number`, which is assessed separately.

number.description: Maximum number of versions of a cell to retain.
number.rationale: Higher values keep more historical versions and can extend recoverable data lifetime (`max_version.number`).

gc_rules.description: Alternative JSON representation of GC rules when not using separate max_age/max_version blocks.
gc_rules.rationale: Alternate syntax for the same GC semantics; the attribute name does not carry secrets. Risk depends on the JSON content you place here, not on choosing this field instead of blocks.

deletion_policy.description: Behavior when deleting the GC policy resource (for example `ABANDON` for replicated instances).
deletion_policy.rationale: Controls how Terraform abandons vs deletes the GC policy resource object; it does not grant IAM on tables or expose cell data by itself.

ignore_warnings.description: If true, allows relaxing GC rules for replicated clusters within documented limits; increases inconsistency risk between replicas.
ignore_warnings.rationale: Not a confidentiality or IAM control: it relaxes GC consistency warnings for replicated clusters and may affect operational consistency, but it does not publish data publicly or add principals by itself.
